residencyRequirements.description: Either party must be domiciled in Northern Ireland at the date the petition is presented, or have been habitually resident in Northern Ireland for at least one year immediately before the petition (Matrimonial Causes (NI) Order 1978, Art.49).

waitingPeriod.description: Decree Nisi can be applied for after the petition has been served and acknowledged (or deemed served). After Decree Nisi is granted, there is a minimum 6-week (42-day) waiting period before applying for Decree Absolute.

noFault.name: 2-Year Separation with Consent
noFault.description: The parties have lived apart for a continuous period of at least two years immediately preceding the petition, and the respondent consents to the granting of the decree.

noFault.name: 5-Year Separation
noFault.description: The parties have lived apart for a continuous period of at least five years immediately preceding the petition. No consent from the respondent is required.

fault.name: Adultery
fault.description: The respondent has, since the date of the marriage, committed adultery. (Unlike England & Wales, there is no additional requirement that the petitioner finds it intolerable to live with the respondent.)

fault.name: Unreasonable Behaviour
fault.description: The respondent has behaved in such a way that the petitioner cannot reasonably be expected to live with the respondent.

fault.name: Desertion for 2 Years
fault.description: The respondent has deserted the petitioner for a continuous period of at least two years immediately preceding the petition.

basic.name: Divorce Petition
basic.description: Initiates the divorce proceeding in the High Court (Family Division) or County Court

basic.name: Statement of Arrangements for Children
basic.description: Required where there are children of the family under 18 — sets out proposed arrangements

basic.name: Affidavit in Support of Petition
basic.description: Sworn affidavit verifying the facts in the petition — required for undefended divorces

basic.name: Ancillary Relief Application
basic.description: Application for financial orders — needed if financial remedy is sought

Welfare of children — welfare principle, Article 8 orders

legalCitations.description: Domestic violence protection — occupation and non-molestation orders
Statutory child maintenance framework — CMS applies UK-wide

filingFees.notes: Filing fee for divorce petition: £310 (per nidirect.gov.uk). A further £117 fee applies for the Decree Absolute (Family Proceedings Fees Schedule, from 1 October 2024). Fee exemption may apply for those receiving certain state benefits or on very low income. A consultation on no-fault divorce ran June-September 2025; no legislation has been enacted as of March 2026.

childSupportGuidelines.guidelines: Child Maintenance Service (CMS) — same UK-wide formula
childSupportGuidelines.notes: CMS uses gross income from HMRC data. Parents may agree private (family-based) arrangements instead.

spousalSupportGuidelines.notes: Court considers all circumstances including income, earning capacity, financial needs, standard of living, age, duration of marriage, disability, and contributions. Discretionary — no fixed formula.

effectiveDateRule: The marriage is dissolved when the Decree Absolute is granted. The Decree Nisi must be granted first, followed by a minimum 6-week waiting period before the petitioner (or 3 months after for the respondent) may apply for the Decree Absolute.
certificateNote: A sealed copy of the Decree Absolute can be obtained from the court. It serves as proof that the marriage has been dissolved.
